I notice the article content appears to be from a publication but lacks a clear publication date in the provided text. Let me fetch additional context if possible — however, since no URL was provided, I'll analyze based solely on the article text.

**Published online:**
Not specified in article text (references events in 2025–2026, suggesting publication ~mid-2026)

**Geographic focus:**
Europe — United Kingdom (Southern England, Cornwall, Devon, Sussex, Scotland; Bay of Biscay referenced)

**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical observation [YES] — cod decline since prior years, seagrass loss since 1930s
T2. Forward-looking immediate [YES] — ongoing 2026 marine heatwave, current species shifts
T3. Long-term development [YES] — climate breakdown, "new normal" framing, 2030 seagrass targets

**Synopsis:**
A 2026 UK marine heatwave — part of an accelerating trend — is reshaping British coastal ecosystems. Cold-water species (cod, mackerel, catshark) are retreating northward or to deeper waters, while warm-water species (sunfish, triggerfish, octopus, mauve stingers) surge. Kelp and seagrass face critical losses. Harmful algal blooms and invasive species add further stress. Fisheries face structural, potentially permanent disruption. Scientists frame repeated marine heatwaves as the "new normal" driven by climate breakdown.
